land.text: Catalonia: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and Tarragona

predecessors.note: Catalonia in 1705; Valencia (1705) and Aragon (1706) follow. The kingdom-of-spain dossier records the matching losses of 1705 and 1706.

successors.note: Majorca, the last land held for the Archduke, falls in June 1715; Catalonia fell with Barcelona on 11 September 1714.

capitals.name: Barcelona
capitals.note: Reading, confidence 2: the pages speak of the 'Allied capture of Barcelona' and an unsuccessful Bourbon attempt to retake it in May 1706 (Almansa page) and of the Archduke's rule being 'limited to the Principality of Catalonia' (Charles VI page); none calls Barcelona the capital. After 11 September 1714 only Majorca was held.

rulers.name: Charles III (Archduke Charles of Austria, later Emperor Charles VI)
rulers.title: claimant King of Spain
rulers.note: The page: he 'disembarked in his kingdom in 1705 and stayed there for six years' and returned to Vienna on his brother Joseph's death (April 1711). Catalan resistance went on without him to 1714-1715; 'Charles finally made peace on 7 March 1714' (Rastatt).

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the whole Crown of Aragon (Catalonia, Aragon, Valencia, the Balearics; 102,406 km2) from 1702, but the page has the Archduke land at Lisbon in March 1704, and the first lands in Spain to go over to him in 1705: 'The 1705 Pact of Genoa between Catalan representatives and Britain opened a second front in the north-east'; the Almansa page puts the Allied capture of Barcelona and Valencia in 1705. Nothing is dated for 1702-1704, so the shape starts in 1705 with Catalonia and Valencia; Aragon and the Balearics follow in 1706. No page gives an area for the claimant's lands, so the 102,406 km2 could not be compared.

keyframe_review.note: The Crown of Aragon in 1706 (Catalonia, Valencia, Aragon after the capture of Zaragoza, the Balearics), without the Madrid and Toledo cells that Cliopatria adds in 1706 and keeps to 1708: the Allied force entered Madrid in 1706 ('his absence allowed an Allied force to capture Madrid and Zaragossa') but 'by November 1706 Philip controlled Castile, Murcia, and parts of Valencia' (War of the Spanish Succession page), so Madrid is an occupation event, not owned land. Cliopatria's 1706-1708 shape is wrong from 1707: Almansa (25 April 1707) and 'by the end of 1707 the Allies were once again restricted to Catalonia and the Balearic Islands'.

correction.text: The Crown of Aragon of the 1702 shape (Catalonia, Aragon, Valencia, the Balearics), for 1706 only

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1707-1714: 'by the end of 1707 the Allies were once again restricted to Catalonia and the Balearic Islands'. Cliopatria ends the row in 1708 but the pages have the Archduke's side holding Catalonia and Majorca to 1714-1715 (the 1710 re-entry into Madrid and Zaragoza is an occupation event). Menorca was captured in 1708 ('the capture of Menorca in 1708') and Great Britain retained it at Utrecht; the pages do not say who held it for the Archduke between, so it stays inside the Balearic cells (unverified).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1715: Barcelona capitulated on 11 September 1714 ('ended Catalan resistance', Catalonia page) and 'Catalonia and Majorca were not finally subdued by the Bourbons until June 1715' (War of the Spanish Succession page; the two pages differ on whether Catalonia held out into 1715). Majorca is the land held to June 1715.

ledger.note: 1705: Catalonia goes over to Archduke Charles as Charles III. 'The 1705 Pact of Genoa between Catalan representatives and Britain opened a second front in the north-east'; the Charles VI page: he 'disembarked in his kingdom in 1705 and stayed there for six years' and his supporters were 'concentrated in the Crown of Aragon'. The claim itself is older: he 'declared himself King of Spain' after Charles II's death (1 November 1700) and landed at Lisbon in March 1704 'to begin a land campaign', with no land in Spain until 1705.

region.text: Catalonia: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and Tarragona

ledger.note: 1705: Valencia is taken for the Archduke. The Almansa page speaks of 'the Allied capture of Barcelona and Valencia' (placed in 1705 by its context; no day). The kingdom-of-spain dossier dates its loss of Aragon and Valencia to 1706 and calls the page silent; the reviewer should settle the year.

region.text: the Valencian provinces of Valencia, Castellón and Alicante

ledger.note: 1706: Aragon goes over to the Archduke. 'His absence allowed an Allied force to capture Madrid and Zaragossa' (Philip was away in 1706). Zaragoza is the page's town; the three provinces are the researcher's reading.

region.text: Aragon: the provinces of Huesca, Zaragoza and Teruel

ledger.note: 1706 (bridging, confidence 1): the Balearic Islands are on the Archduke's side. The Almansa page says only that 'by the end of 1707 the Allies were once again restricted to Catalonia and the Balearic Islands'; Cliopatria draws them from 1702.

1706: Allied troops enter Madrid. 'His absence allowed an Allied force to capture Madrid and Zaragossa'; the War of the Spanish Succession page: an Allied force from Portugal entered Madrid after Philip's absence in May 1706. Cliopatria's 1706-1708 shape includes Madrid and Toledo cells for three years; the page has the city back in Bourbon hands within the year.
1706: Madrid is lost again. 'By November 1706 Philip controlled Castile, Murcia, and parts of Valencia' (the page gives a bound, not a day).

25 April 1707: Almansa. 'The Battle of Almansa took place on 25 April 1707'; 'the Franco-Spanish army quickly over-ran Valencia and besieged Xàtiva' (which surrendered in June); 'by the end of 1707 the Allies were once again restricted to Catalonia and the Balearic Islands'. The page does not mention Aragon by name.

ledger.note: 1710: the Archduke re-enters Madrid. 'Archduke Charles re-entered Madrid in 1710 after victories at Almenar and Saragossa.' Occupation, not owned land.
10 December 1710: Villaviciosa. 'The Battle of Villaviciosa on 10 December confirmed Bourbon control of Spain.'

11 September 1714: Barcelona falls. The Catalonia page: 'The siege and capitulation of Barcelona (11 September 1714) ended Catalan resistance.' The War of the Spanish Succession page has Catalonia and Majorca 'not finally subdued by the Bourbons until June 1715'; the kingdom-of-spain dossier dates Catalonia's gain to June 1715 from that page.

ledger.note: June 1715: Majorca, the last land held for the Archduke, is subdued. 'Catalonia and Majorca were not finally subdued by the Bourbons until June 1715' (the page's own end of the war after the Treaty of Baden of 7 September 1714). The Nueva Planta decrees follow (page: 'Catalonia and Majorca remained outside the system until 1767').

wars.outcome: Philip V is recognised as king of Spain (Utrecht, 11 April 1713, which Austria did not sign); Charles 'finally made peace on 7 March 1714'; Treaty of Baden 7 September 1714; Catalonia and Majorca 'not finally subdued by the Bourbons until June 1715'.
wars.note: Infobox 'March 1701 - 7 September 1714'. Spain ceded Milan, the Spanish Netherlands, Naples and Sardinia to Austria and Sicily to Savoy; those lands are in the kingdom-of-spain and habsburg-monarchy dossiers, not in this row.

notes:
Pro-Habsburg Spain (Cliopatria 1702-1708), the Spain of Archduke Charles (Charles III). Pages: War of the Spanish Succession, Charles VI, Battle of Almansa (one over the 1-2 page budget, opened for the 1707 loss) plus the Catalonia page opened for the catalonia dossier. The Cliopatria Wikipedia title, 'Habsburg Spain', is the article on the Spanish Habsburgs of 1516-1700 and was not opened.

Corrections to Cliopatria: the row begins in 1702 with the whole Crown of Aragon, but the pages put the Archduke's first lands in 1705 (Catalonia; Valencia by the Almansa page's context) and 1706 (Aragon); the row ends in 1708 although Catalonia and Majorca held out to 1714-1715; the 1706-1708 shape keeps Madrid and Toledo cells that the pages have Bourbon again within 1706; from 1707 the lands are Catalonia and the Balearic Islands. I set the state 1705 to June 1715 and gave new keyframes for 1707-1714 and 1715.

Disagreements and gaps: (1) The kingdom-of-spain dossier dates the loss of Aragon and Valencia to 1706 (confidence 1), and its gain of Catalonia and Majorca to June 1715; this dossier dates Valencia to 1705 (Almansa page, context), Barcelona's fall to 11 September 1714 (Catalonia page) and Majorca to June 1715 (War of the Spanish Succession page, which lumps Catalonia into June 1715 against the Catalonia page). (2) The pages do not say who held Menorca between its capture in 1708 and Utrecht. (3) The pages do not say when the Balearics declared for the Archduke. (4) No infobox area for the claimant; the Cliopatria areas could not be compared. (5) The ruler strip has one claimant only; the Catalan institutions that fought on after 1711 are not on the pages opened. A gap-filler should open the Siege of Barcelona (1713-1714), the Treaty of Utrecht and the Nueva Planta decrees.
